nodes.label: End user
nodes.summary: Signs in, opens and shares documents, photos or projects.

nodes.label: Identity provider
nodes.summary: Authenticates the user and issues an OpenID Connect ID Token (a JWT with claims about the authentication) plus OAuth 2.0 access and refresh tokens.

nodes.label: API gateway
nodes.summary: Verifies token signature, audience and expiry locally with the issuer's public key and passes the user id on. Our reference design.

nodes.label: Client application
nodes.summary: A product service (Drive, Photos, YouTube at Google) that stores content and asks the permissions service before acting.

nodes.label: Content store
nodes.summary: The client's own storage; it saves each content version together with its zookie in one atomic write.

nodes.label: Zanzibar
nodes.summary: Global authorization service: trillions of ACLs, millions of checks per second, p95 under 10 ms, above 99.999% availability (2019).

nodes.label: aclservers
nodes.summary: Answer Check, Read, Expand and Write; fan out within the cluster to walk userset rewrites and nested groups; evaluate at a snapshot at least as fresh as the zookie.

nodes.label: Check cache
nodes.summary: Distributed cache of reads and (intermediate) check results across the cluster, placed by consistent hashing; deduplicates simultaneous requests.

nodes.label: watchservers
nodes.summary: Tail the changelog and stream namespace changes to clients in near real time.

nodes.label: Tuple store (Spanner)
nodes.summary: One database of relation tuples per namespace, one of namespace configs, one shared changelog; TrueTime timestamps give external consistency and bounded-staleness snapshot reads.

nodes.label: Leopard index
nodes.summary: Indexing system for large, deeply nested sets: reads snapshots, watches changes, denormalises group membership.

nodes.label: Access-aware index
nodes.summary: A client's secondary index (for example search) kept in sync through the Watch API.

steps.caption: The user signs in and receives an ID Token and a short-lived access token.
The request carries the access token.
The gateway verifies it locally and passes the user id to the app.
The app asks whether the user is a viewer of the doc, passing the zookie stored with the content.
Rewrite rules expand viewer to editors, owners and parent-folder viewers; cached sub-results answer most of it.
Anything missing is read at a snapshot at least as fresh as the zookie, usually from a local replica.

flows.name: Saving content with a consistency token

steps.caption: Before saving, the app makes a content-change check and gets a zookie newer than all prior ACL writes.
It stores the new content and the zookie in one atomic write.
Tuple changes are appended to the changelog.
The client's index receives them through Watch and updates who can see what.
Alice removes Bob from a doc, then Charlie adds new content, saved with a fresh zookie.
Bob's check carries that zookie, so it must use a snapshot that already includes his removal; a stale replica is not allowed.
Many checks hit objects shared with one popular group at once.
Identical requests are deduplicated and timestamps quantised so they share cache entries.
Deep group membership comes from the denormalised Leopard index; slow backend calls are hedged.
